correctness.rationale: Full proof checked from definitions: eigenvalue-difference majorization and scalar strict-convex KKT ensure unique p-independent map; p=2 Hilbert nonexpansivity; traceless n=2 and n=3 quartic identities yield the extra contractive cases; every excluded pair has an analytic local expansive perturbation. The n=3 key matrix has eigenvalues golden-ratio, -1 and inverse negative; its directional Schatten-p derivative is nonzero precisely off p=2,4, and the spectral projection derivative converges to its norm-expanding range vector as delta tends to zero. Finite tests: 25 quartic, 150 nonexpansive, 14 expansive, independently supplemented by explicit differential calculations. No endpoint p=1,infty or exact expansive constant claimed.

value.rationale: The precise nonexpansive norm and dimension phase boundary is a natural stability question for repairing trace-one, possibly nonphysical quantum estimators. The exceptional n=3,p=4 holds for all noncommuting traceone inputs, while explicit noncommuting perturbations prove all other n3 cases fail; diagonal dimension-four witnesses prove sharpness for all higher dimensions. This is a complete meaningful structural classification, not a routine scalar simplex computation.
